answer: Whether an agent maps a canyon, tracks a falcon, or writes a sonnet, each concurrent job requires a fixed bond locked until verification ends. Creating extra identities cannot increase working capacity without extra collateral: ten identities taking ten jobs must post ten bonds. A result that fails the job’s agreed, machine-checkable test forfeits its bond. A sybil swarm therefore ties up capital for every active job and loses that capital on verifiably invalid work.
